## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d63d5ea2163e8de76d219629b738b8091cba68cf`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .github/workflows/stale.yml + none

Read at 2026-11-15T19:08Z. First review of this head, taken on patrol as owed; claim: comment 6899654789. Independence: implemented in an os-steve project thread; neither dispatched nor implemented by os-tesla.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The diff is what the PR says.** Net diff against merge base `fb79d47c` is one file, +2/-1: `exempt-issue-labels` goes from `'pinned,security,roadmap,tracking'` to `'pinned,security,roadmap,tracking,governed-merges-audit'`, and one comment line is added above it. Every other key of the step is byte-identical: the `uses: actions/stale@v11.0.0` pin, `permissions`, `timeout-minutes`, the cron, both day pairs, `exempt-pr-labels`, `operations-per-run`, `remove-stale-when-updated`.
- **The label is spelled as the card carries it.** `fleet-patrols.yml` at this head, job `governed-merges-audit`, sets `ANCHOR_IDENTITY_LABEL: governed-merges-audit` (L1632) and the card step files with `labels: [identityLabel, stateLabel]` (L1851) through `issues.create`. The string in `stale.yml` matches it character for character. A refresh rewrites the body only and never the labels, and the job header says the identity label is never graded off, so the label stays on the card for its whole open life.
- **List syntax.** `actions/stale` reads `exempt-issue-labels` as one comma-separated string; the new entry is appended inside the same quoted scalar, with no space and no trailing comma, the shape the four existing entries already use.
- **`exempt-pr-labels` needs nothing.** The audit card is an issue only: it is minted by `issues.create`, and the anchor lookup filters with `!i.pull_request`. No PR ever carries the label.
- **The claimed harm is real, read in the code.** `composeAuditCard` carries BREACH rows only from an OPEN card (`existing`); a closed card is never reopened, and a stale-bot close rules nothing (`auditCloseRuling`, self-test row `the-stale-bot`). So a stale close would leave rows outside the 7-day window on no open card and unruled.
- **Card acceptance.** `exempt-issue-labels` names `governed-merges-audit`: met. `skip-changeset`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`: on the PR. Draft, Tier H, left for a GOVERNED_APPROVERS merge: as the seat's ACCEPT records. The comment clause the card asked for is there. "The workflow lints green": see ②.
- **No other gate reads the changed key.** At this head the only readers of `stale.yml` are `scripts/pm/mailbox-open.mjs` (its self-test reads `exempt-pr-labels` for `pinned`, untouched), `check-half-states.mjs` (a fixture of its own) and `dispatch-gates.self-test.mjs` (the trigger list, untouched). `ensure-pm-labels.sh` documents `pinned` and `work-in-progress` as exemption labels and says nothing that this edit makes false. No AGENTS.md roster names the exempt list.

### ② Semver level

None. A repo workflow input; nothing published, `skip-changeset` is right, `Clause-②: no` holds (no schema, no consumer-visible behaviour).

CI on `d63d5ea2`: 57 check-runs, 31 success, 26 skipped, 0 failed, 0 in progress, 0 queued. All ten Lint contexts (repo gates, CI/release/engine gates, PM dispatch-gates, tooling self-tests among them) are green. Nothing is still running, so the seat has nothing to wait for. ⚠️ `stale.yml` is `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` only: no check on this head executes the edited step, so "lints green" is the static reading, which is all a PR can give for this file.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The label does not exist in the repo today.** `GET /labels/governed-merges-audit` answers 404 and no issue, open or closed, carries it: the audit has not filed a card yet. That is not a defect of this PR. `issues.create` with the job's `issues: write` token mints a missing label on the first card, so the exemption is live from the first card on. It is worth knowing because `ensure-pm-labels.sh` records the opposite outcome for `pinned` and `work-in-progress` (hand-applied labels that answered 404 made their exemption dead); this label is machine-applied on create, so that failure does not repeat here. `roadmap` in the same list also answers 404 today; pre-existing, out of scope.
- **The sibling anchor has the same exposure.** The `platform-checklist-watchdog` card (`ANCHOR_IDENTITY_LABEL: platform-checklist-watchdog`, routing `pm:queue,tooling`) carries no exempt label either. Outside this card's surface; a triage call, not a finding on this diff.
- **Governed path.** `.github/workflows/stale.yml` is Tier H (`job:stale` holds `issues: write` and `pull-requests: write`). The edit widens nothing the token can do: it only makes the bot skip more issues.

### ④ Design judgment

`.github/workflows/stale.yml` against the code it cites (`fleet-patrols.yml` and `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` at this head, read, not reviewed) and the card's scenario: the change holds. The exemption names the one label the card is guaranteed to carry while open, and it closes the route by which a non-ruling close could take carried BREACH rows off every open card.

- S1 (should-fix) — The new comment, the PR body and the card all name a DEAD patrol as the trigger ("so a dead patrol's card would close"; the card: while the patrol is alive the card "is refreshed every week"). The code says otherwise: the card step's `if:` skips the whole step on a `clean` verdict, and `composeAuditCard` is documented as never called on one. So an open, unruled card is left untouched through every clean week of a HEALTHY patrol, and 60 quiet days plus 14 would stale-close it with the patrol running. The exemption is right and covers this case too; the stated reason is narrower than the real one, and a reader who later gives the patrol a heartbeat could conclude the exemption is no longer needed. Fix in the comment: say the card is refreshed only on a BREACH or NOT MEASURED week, so a run of clean weeks, or a stopped patrol, leaves it untouched. Not blocking: the behaviour shipped is correct.
- N1 (nit) — Nothing pins that the string in `exempt-issue-labels` equals the job's `ANCHOR_IDENTITY_LABEL`; a rename of the identity label would silently kill the exemption. `mailbox-open.mjs` pins `pinned` against `exempt-pr-labels` in its self-test, so there is precedent, but `tracking` has no such pin and the card did not ask for one. The PR body's "no test pins this workflow key" is accurate. A follow-up at the seat's discretion.

No must-fix.
